title: Formula width fold
statement: Let $\varphi$ be a finite CNF formula over variables indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, and let $g$ be a Boolean flag. Folding the width-pass transition over the binary encoding of $\varphi$, starting in state $0$ with counter $0$ and flag $g$, ends in state $4$ with counter $0$ and flag $g\wedge W(\varphi)$, where $W(\varphi)$ is true exactly when every clause of $\varphi$ has at most three literal occurrences. In particular, the empty formula passes this test.
hypotheses_covered: $\varphi$ is a CNF formula over natural-number-indexed variables
replaced:
Folding the width-pass transition over the serialization of a CNF formula
$\varphi$ from the initial state ends at the exact-end position with counter zero
and the goodness flag conjoined with the Boolean width-three test of $\varphi$;
every clause is checked and the empty formula passes vacuously.
